Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU pool + regional planning for SolveSky

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency and cost controls. We're ready to start the Dedicated onboarding process and want to lock down two things quickly so we can finish the SOW: regional capacity selection (US primary, possibly EU failover) and the autoscale/burst policy we should plan for initial provisioning.

Baseline info:
- Expected production QPS: 650 inference requests/min (steady), peaks up to ~2,500 req/min during batch campaigns (~5 hours, twice/week)
- Average request length: 350 tokens output per request
- Initial model: redwood/gpt-large-v1 (quantized)
- Data residency: US-only for now, EU planned in Q4

Two asks for tomorrow's call:
1) Recommended pool size for steady-plus-burst with a 99th pct latency target of 200ms.
2) A proposed burst policy (how much reserve vs autoscale latency tradeoffs) and how cross-region fallback would look (if EU region isn't warm).

I've attached a quick capacity profile (SolveSky_capacity_profile.xlsx) and a couple sample traffic snippets. Can you confirm who from your side should be on the technical call?

Thanks,
Tom Becker
Head of Platform — SolveSky AI

Attachments: SolveSky_capacity_profile.xlsx, traffic-sample-snippets.jsonl

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Thanks — quick technical notes before the call:

1) Sizing approach (high level):
- Steady-state: size for the 650 req/min steady (assume optimal batching, average 350 tokens -> estimate ~3 concurrent generations per request on average).
- Burst headroom: we recommend capacity to cover 2x steady (1,300 req/min) in the dedicated pool and carve an autoscale runway to absorb spikes to 2,500 with short warm-up (spin-up + prefix cache warm period).

2) Autoscale & burst policy options to discuss:
- Conservative: Provision steady pool + 1.5x reserved burst (fast fallback to smaller models if warm cache missing). Pros: lower cold-surge latencies for predictable bursts. Cons: higher committed cost.
- Cost-first: Keep lower steady, rely on autoscale to add on-demand nodes. Pros: saves cost; Cons: higher 95/99 latency during cold bursts.
- Hybrid (recommended): Moderate steady pool, low-cost pre-warmed spare nodes for short bursts, plus aggressive autoscale to 2.5k with staged scaling (fast add of small instances + larger instances to follow).

3) Regional fallback pattern:
- Primary: us-west (PDT) pool. Failover: us-east for capacity and eu-west as long-run (if EU residency permitted needs separate setup).
- Warm/cold implications: cross-region fallback will incur tokenization/kvcache miss and network egress latency; plan SLO relaxation for regional fallback.

Prep request: can you share a 24-hour sample (line-level) and a weekly peak day trace? That will let us produce a recommended node count and a simulated latency curve.

I'll draft a short decision matrix and bring it to the call.

—Karthik
Infra PM, Dedicated Capacity — Redwood Inference
